title: Follow-Up Sequences
subtitle: The sale rarely happens on the first contact, build thes ystem that closes later
useWhen: You send one follow-up after a meeting or proposal and then give up if you hear nothing. You assume silence means no. But most deals are decided after the fifth or sixth touchpoint and you're stopping at two.
howToUse: Research in B2B sales consistently shows that 80% of sales require five or more follow- ups, yet 44% of salespeople give up after one. A follow-up sequence is a multi-touch, multi-channel cadence of value-adding contacts that keeps you visible without being pushy. Each touch should add something new, a relevant insight, a case study, an answer to an unanswered question rather than asking 'just checking in.' AI can build an entire sequence for a specific deal in minutes.
steps: Never follow up with 'just checking in' every touch must add value.
Vary the channel: email, LinkedIn, phone, voice note, video message.
Space touches 3–5 business days apart in the first two weeks, then weekly.

Build a break-up email for touch 6 or 7 it often gets the highest response rate. Don't let AI turn your follow-ups into spam. A sequence built in minutes still needs your judgment before it sends. If touch three reads like touch one with new words swapped in, the prospect notices before you do. Persistence without a real reason to reach out reads as pressure, not value and pressure gets you blocked, not booked
origin: B2B sales research — follow-up cadence methodology, widely documented 2010s
promptBody:
Act as a B2B sales sequence strategist.
Deal context        :  [WHAT YOU PROPOSED AND WHAT THEY SAID]
Prospect role      :  [JOB TITLE AND INDUSTRY]
Last contact        :  [WHAT HAPPENED IN YOUR LAST INTERACTION]
Build a 7-touch follow-up sequence:
Touch 1 (Day 1)    :  Post-meeting summary and one insight
Touch 2 (Day 3)   :  Relevant content or case study
Touch 3 (Day 6)   :  Answer a question they didn't ask yet
Touch 4 (Day 10) :  Social proof specific to their industry
Touch 5 (Day 15) :  New angle  challenge their status quo
Touch 6 (Day 22) :  Offer to simplify or reduce scope
Touch 7 (Day 30) :  Break-up email  honest and respectful
For each touch    :  write the subject line and opening sentence.
Keep every message under 60 words.

proTip:
The break-up email (Touch 7) consistently generates the highest reply rate of any touch
in a sequence. Something about 'I'm going to stop reaching out' creates a response that
seven other emails didn't. Write it genuinely  not as a manipulation tactic. If you really
are moving on, say so honestly.
